D000798.s: A condition with multiple tumor-like lesions caused either by congenital or developmental malformations of blood vessels, or reactive vascular proliferations, such as in bacillary angiomatosis. Angiomatosis is considered non-neoplastic.

D001168.s: Acute or chronic inflammation of joints.

D001638.s: A form of supportive psychotherapy in which the patient is given carefully selected material to read.

D001753.s: Injuries resulting when a person is struck by particles impelled with violent force from an explosion. Blast causes pulmonary concussion and hemorrhage, laceration of other thoracic and abdominal viscera, ruptured ear drums, and minor effects in the central nervous system. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

D002590.s: Infections with true tapeworms of the helminth subclass cestoda.

D003258.s: Behavior associated with the procurement of goods, services, or experiences.

D003320.s: Loss of epithelial tissue from the surface of the cornea due to progressive erosion and necrosis of the tissue; usually caused by bacterial, fungal, or viral infection.

D004620.s: Blocking of a blood vessel by fat deposits in the circulation. It is often seen after fractures of large bones or after administration of corticosteroids.

D005263.s: The main artery of the thigh, a continuation of the external iliac artery.

D005533.s: Skin diseases of the foot, general or unspecified.

D006352.s: The lower right and left chambers of the heart. The right ventricle pumps venous blood into the lungs and the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the systemic arterial circulation.

D006525.s: Inflammation of the liver in humans due to infection by viruses. There are several significant types of human viral hepatitis with infection caused by enteric-transmission (hepatitis A; hepatitis E) or blood transfusion (hepatitis B; hepatitis C; and hepatitis D).

D006824.s: The genetic process of crossbreeding between genetically dissimilar parents to produce a hybrid.

D008053.s: Lipolysis of stored lipids in the adipose tissue to release free fatty acids. Mobilization of stored lipids is under the regulation of lipolytic signals (catecholamines) or anti-lipolytic signals (insulin) via their actions on the hormone-sensitive lipase.

e: Descending Limb of Loop of Henle
Ascending Limb of Loop of Henle
D008138.s: The U-shaped portion of the renal tubule in the kidney medulla, consisting of a descending limb and an ascending limb. It is situated between the proximal kidney tubule and the distal kidney tubule.

D008888.s: The practice of nursing in military environments.

D009630.s: The failure of homologous chromosomes or chromatids to segregate during mitosis or meiosis with the result that one daughter cell has both of a pair of parental chromosomes or chromatids and the other has none.

D009807.s: Cysts found in the jaws and arising from epithelium involved in tooth formation. They include follicular cysts (e.g., primordial cyst, dentigerous cyst, multilocular cyst), lateral periodontal cysts, and radicular cysts. They may become keratinized (odontogenic keratocysts).

D010272.s: Infections or infestations with parasites. They are often contracted through contact with an intermediate vector, but may occur as the result of direct exposure.

D010319.s: A disease of pregnant and lactating cows and ewes leading to generalized paresis and death. The disease, which is characterized by hypocalcemia, occurs at or shortly after parturition in cows and within weeks before or after parturition in ewes.

D010975.s: Drugs or agents which antagonize or impair any mechanism leading to blood platelet aggregation, whether during the phases of activation and shape change or following the dense-granule release reaction and stimulation of the prostaglandin-thromboxane system.

D011114.s: The collective name for the islands of the central Pacific Ocean, including the Austral Islands, Cook Islands, Easter Island, hawaii; new zealand; Phoenix Islands, pitcairn island; samoa; tonga; Tuamotu Archipelago, Wake Island, and Wallis and Futuna Islands.

D011811.s: Five individuals derived from five fetuses that were fertilized at or about the same time, developed in the uterus simultaneously, and born to the same mother.

D011864.s: Radioimmunoassay of proteins using antibody coupled to an immunosorbent.

D012708.s: Supporting cells projecting inward from the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules. They surround and nourish the developing male germ cells and secrete the androgen-binding protein and hormones such as ANTI-mullerian hormone.

D013156.s: Surgical procedure involving either partial or entire removal of the spleen.

D013350.s: The continuation of the axillary vein which follows the subclavian artery and then joins the internal jugular vein to form the brachiocephalic vein.

D013606.s: Parenchymatous neurosyphilis marked by slowly progressive degeneration of the posterior columns, posterior roots, and ganglia of the spinal cord.

D013817.s: Imaging the temperatures in a material, or in the body or an organ. Imaging is based on self-emanating infrared radiation (heat waves), or on changes in properties of the material or tissue that vary with temperature, such as elasticity; magnetic field; or luminescence.

D015594.s: Optic disk bodies composed primarily of acid mucopolysaccharides that may produce pseudopapilledema (elevation of the optic disk without associated intracranial hypertension) and visual field deficits. Drusen may also occur in the retina (see retinal drusen).

D016586.s: Unusual tumor affecting any site of the body, but most often encountered in the head and neck. Considerable debate has surrounded the histogenesis of this neoplasm; however, it is considered to be a myoblastoma of, usually, a benign nature. It affects women more often than men.

D017321.n: Clinical Trials, Phase I as Topic
e: Drug Evaluation, FDA Phase I as Topic
D017321.s: Works about studies performed to evaluate the safety of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques in healthy subjects and to determine the safe dosage range (if appropriate).

D017354.s: A mutation caused by the substitution of one nucleotide for another. This results in the DNA molecule having a change in a single base pair.

D017619.s: Irradiation of one half or both halves of the body in the treatment of disseminated cancer or widespread metastases. It is used to treat diffuse metastases in one session as opposed to multiple fields over an extended period.

D017772.s: Disorders of the peripheral nervous system associated with the deposition of amyloid in nerve tissue. Familial, primary (nonfamilial), and secondary forms have been described. Some familial subtypes demonstrate an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance.

D018166.s: Innovation and improvement of the health care system by reappraisal, amendment of services, and removal of faults and abuses in providing and distributing health services to patients.

D019275.s: Compounds that are used in medicine as sources of radiation for radiotherapy and for diagnostic purposes. They have numerous uses in research and industry. (Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p1161)

D019819.s: A glucocorticoid used in the management of asthma, the treatment of various skin disorders, and allergic rhinitis.

D020239.s: The simultaneous or sequential binding of multiple cell surface receptors to different ligands resulting in coordinated stimulation or suppression of signal transduction.

e: Parkinson Disease Autosomal Recessive, Early Onset
Parkinsonism, Early Onset, with Diurnal Fluctuation
D020734.s: A group of disorders which feature impaired motor control characterized by bradykinesia, muscle rigidity; tremor; and postural instability.

D021801.s: The joint that occurs between facets of the interior and superior articular processes of adjacent vertebrae.

D035844.s: Interaction between research personnel and research subjects.

D041641.s: The morphologic and physiological changes of the muscles, bones (bone and bones), and cartilage of the body, i.e., musculoskeletal system, during the prenatal and postnatal stages of development.

D045483.s: Large natural streams of fresh water formed by converging tributaries and which empty into a body of water (lake or ocean).

D056267.s: A distinct variant of mycosis fungoides characterized by the presence of localized patches or plaques with an intraepidermal proliferation of neoplastic cells.

D058430.s: The upper rounded extremity of the humerus fitting into the glenoid cavity of the scapula.

D063586.s: Evaluation of the degree of acceptance for the immediate variables associated with a procedure or program designed to change behavior.

D000068736.s: A thiophene derivative and selective neurotransmitter uptake inhibitor for serotonin and noradrenaline (SNRI). It is an antidepressive agent and anxiolytic, and is also used for the treatment of pain in patients with diabetes mellitus and fibromyalgia.

D000077765.s: A general term which describes a group of rare eye disorders that affect the cone cells of the retina.

D000092162.s: Crystals in the urine found in urinary sediment analysis. Urinary crystalline may be formed from various metabolites (e.g. Calcium oxalates; calcium phosphates; urates) and drugs (e.g., sulphadiazine; acyclovir; and triamterene).

D000097103.s: Use of digital technologies in medicine and other health professions to manage illnesses and health risks and to promote wellness; includes the use of wearable devices; health information technology; electronic health records; telemedicine; and personalized medicine.

D000097873.s: The generation of images of the body's structures, organs, and tissues after death.

D000099196.s: A signal transduction pathway that involves cGMP-AMP synthase (cGAS), stimulator of interferon genes (sting), and downstream signaling adaptors. This pathway plays an essential role in the innate immune system by activating immune defenses, particularly against invading pathogens or harmful damage.
